guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: utilisation target, overtime hours, clawback days and share, spiff, employer extras and cash floor. Pay figures: confirm with your adviser.
Check Team: one row per person with role, pay type, hourly rate or salary, hours a week and commission percent. Everything else reads this sheet.
Type each week of hours on Timesheets: clock, billed, drive, shop and idle hours, overtime and pay. Utilisation, idle cost and the unbilled labour cost fill in by themselves.
Add every pay run to Payroll. Hours by Week and Capacity by Week add up the crew for you.
Fill Commission Statements with the sold and collected work, the agreements sold and the clawback bases of each month. Commission, spiffs, clawback and the total fill in by themselves.
Keep the Spiff List and the Commission Rules to your own numbers, and record every Callback so the clawback follows.
Type the jobs and revenue of the last 12 months on Scorecard by Technician. Jobs, Estimates and Reviews and Referrals feed ticket, close rate, callback rate and reviews.
Add leave and training days on Leave and Training; Capacity by Week takes them off the available hours.

Use the 18 tools: hours analysis, the paid versus billed gap, pay and commission calculators, clawback, statements, scorecards, overtime, capacity, hire break-even, apprentice ramp and the payroll forecast.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
A shop with one technician and one apprentice uses the same sheets: type two people on Team and Timesheets.
Read the KPI Dashboard and Charts every Monday: utilisation, idle cost, overtime, payroll, commission, capacity gap and weeks over capacity.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Technician Hours, Pay, Commission and Capacity Excel Template: Utilisation, Spiffs, Clawbacks, Hire Break-Even
listing.headline: Know what every technician hour costs and when to hire
listing.description:
Run the people side of an HVAC and plumbing business in one Excel workbook. Built for a small owner-run service shop with 1 to 15 technicians, or an owner-operator with one technician and one apprentice.

Timesheets hold the hours of every person each week: clock, billed, drive, shop and idle hours, overtime, pay and loaded cost. Utilisation (billed hours over hours on the clock), the cost of idle time and the paid-but-unbilled gap in money fill in by themselves, with a weekly view against your own target and the same week last year.

The Pay Calculator and the Pay Model Comparison work out hourly, flat-rate, salary plus commission and mixed pay, with overtime and employer extras from Settings, the all-in cost per clock hour and per billed hour, and the model that is cheapest for the shop. Commission Statements calculate commission on sold or collected work, spiffs (a fixed bonus for each item sold) and clawbacks (a commission amount taken back after a callback or an unpaid invoice), and the Technician Statement prints one month a person can read.

The Technician Scorecard puts ticket, close rate, callback rate, utilisation, revenue per day and reviews against each technician's own history, with points, rank and a verdict for the one-to-one talk. Capacity by Week sets booked hours against the hours your people can work after leave, with the season in mind; the Capacity and Hire Tool, the Hire Break-Even Solver and the Apprentice Ramp tell you whether to hire a technician or an apprentice, now or before the season, and how many extra jobs a week it takes to pay for the hire. The Payroll Cost Forecast shows the next 13 weeks with Base, Best and Worst rows and the effect on your cash floor.

18 tools, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages to technicians, apprentices, the office manager, the owner, your accountant and your insurance agent are included.

This is part four of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data. Pay, overtime and tax figures are examples: confirm them with your adviser. It helps you keep track of hours, pay and capacity and does not promise results.

competitors.what: field-service app with a per-technician fee
competitors.lacks: charges every month per person and keeps pay and commission rules hidden, so you cannot test a pay model or a clawback rule yourself
adds up hours and pay but knows nothing about billed hours, drive time, idle cost or a commission with a clawback
collects hours only, with no utilisation against a target, no overtime warning and no link to jobs and revenue
keeps no history, so idle time, callbacks per technician and the cost of an unbilled hour are never counted
lists questions but never works out the jobs a week a new technician must bring to pay for the hire
